concerns.text: T006 says Wilcoxon tests run 'on per-sample errors', but plan.md's Statistical Analysis Plan says tests run on 'the vector of per-sample ECE values and on the vector of Sharpness values', and stats.schema.yaml's metric_type enum is only calibration_error|sharpness. The implementer cannot determine what vector is fed to the test (abs_error? per-sample ECE? sharpness?) — name the exact input column/derivation and which metric_type values appear in the report.

All tasks write outputs to `data/results/` while plan.md and data-model.md specify `results/` (e.g. `results/uq_methods.csv`, `results/sensitivity_conformal.csv` vs T007's `data/results/sensitivity_report.csv`). An implementer following the plan vs the tasks produces different paths; T011's handoff test would then fail. Pick one convention and state it in the tasks.

'(and interval-producing equivalents for the other methods where applicable)' is not executable — 'where applicable' is undefined. Specify exactly which methods are swept (e.g. conformal only, or all four with quantile-scaled intervals) so test_sensitivity.py's expected row count is deterministic.

T008 mandates 'abort on limit breach' for model-constraint violations, while NFR-002 requires partial results saved when some methods fail and T004's uq_methods registry has a `failed` status. As written, an implementer cannot satisfy both abort-on-violation and partial-results; specify which failures abort vs. which are logged and recorded as `status=failed`.

T004 is coarse: it spans pipeline extension, four model integrations, three registry/log CSVs, and cost metrics in one task. Flag for the atomizer to split (e.g. per-method training tasks + orchestration/registry task).
T001's verification is 'a short Python check' with no named file or command. Name it (e.g. `code/tests/test_schema_columns.py`) so done-ness is checkable.
